name: Shared strings (the design system's placeholders, final)

rows.w: The top bar's Display button: its name and tooltip
rows.t: Already a verb-free noun phrase naming the menu's contents; kept.

rows.w: Display menu: the first group's label
Display menu: the first Theme item (the others are Light and Dark)
rows.t: "System" also means the admin scope; this says what the choice does.

rows.w: Display menu: the switch's label, the same in both positions

rows.o: Your device asks for reduced motion
rows.n: Your device is set to reduce motion, so Kiwi stays still.
rows.w: Display menu: the inert Kiwi animation switch's reason
rows.t: States the reason and its effect (the disabled-reason pattern).

rows.n: Your browser won't save this setting, so it resets when you reload the page.
rows.w: Display menu: the caption when local storage is unavailable
rows.t: What happened, why, and what it means. When storage is blocked the choice lives in memory, so it lasts until the page is reloaded; "for the session" in `§ The Display menu` means this. The caption does not say "until you close this tab": a reload also clears it.

rows.n: Kiwi is answering. Select Stop to interrupt.
rows.w: Chat composer: the reason the field is disabled while an answer streams
Chat composer: the Stop control's accessible name (its visible label is "Stop")
Feedback toolbar: Regenerate's reason (a toggletip)
rows.t: A reason specific to its control, never a page label.

rows.w: Feedback toolbar: Share's reason (a toggletip)
PDF toolbar: the chip on the page Kiwi has in context
rows.t: "In context" is a developer phrase; the chat does receive that page's text.

rows.w: A code block's Copy button: its accessible name (the visible label stays "Copy", then "Copied")
rows.t: The button is `CopyButton.tsx`, which draws the visible label "Copy", then "Copied"; only its accessible name changes. `CopyButton.test.tsx:38` queries the visible text (`getByText('Copy')`) and keeps passing; a query by role and name would use "Copy code".

rows.w: Table footer: Previous's reason on page 1
Table footer: Next's reason on the last page

rows.o: Professors are removed by an admin
rows.n: Only an administrator can remove instructors.
rows.w: Table: the reason a row cannot be removed
Table and DataGrid: the error alert in the body slot (a pattern; each page's own message is in its route's rows)
KPI tile: the value slot in the error state, beside Retry
Text action in an alert, a toast or an error frame: one verb
Text action in an alert, a toast or the banner: one verb
Text action in a toast after a reversible removal: one verb
A busy control's label: an -ing verb and the ellipsis character (Creating…, Sending… follow the same form)
A copy button's two-second success label
Empty-state frame, first use: the heading (a pattern)
Empty-state frame, first use, for a role that can act: its one primary button

rows.n: {Who acts} adds {things}. They will appear here.
rows.w: Empty-state frame, no-action variant: the copy says who acts and when (never a disabled button)
Empty-state frame, no results: the heading, naming the search

rows.n: Check the spelling, or search for another name.
rows.w: Empty-state frame, no results: the copy
Empty-state frame, load error: the heading, above the cause line and Retry
rows.t: The error form of the empty-state frame: this heading is followed by the cause line and Retry (C12).

rows.n: Your account doesn't have access to this page
rows.w: Reserved for the Stage 2 fix of B4: the no-permission state's heading (the state does not exist on this branch). The access-control branch (`fix/access-control`) adds it as `auth/NoPermission.tsx`, reading "You don't have permission to view this page"; on merge these two strings replace that wording, and a refused permission uses them (not S-05.06)

rows.n: Ask an administrator if you need it.
rows.w: Reserved for the Stage 2 fix of B4: the no-permission state's copy; with the heading above it replaces the wording `fix/access-control` adds
Confirmation dialog: the title, a question that names the object (a pattern)

rows.n: {What happens to it}. {Whether it can be undone.}
rows.w: Confirmation dialog: the body, consequence first, then permanence (a pattern)

rows.o: You do not have permission to perform this action.
rows.why: Your account doesn't have access to it.
rows.m: You do not have permission to perform this action.
rows.w: Native alert from the shared request middleware on any 403 (SF-11): copy only. It applies until the access-control merge (branch `fix/access-control`): that branch removes this alert (a 403 no longer signs out or alerts), and a refused permission then shows the page's own `denied` error or the no-permission state (DS.29, DS.30)
rows.t: A native alert shown on every 403; the words say what and who to ask.

rows.o: The requested resource was not found.
rows.why: It may have been deleted or moved.
rows.m: The requested resource was not found.
rows.w: Native alert from the shared request middleware on any 404 (SF-11): copy only

rows.o: Enter at least one email first
rows.w: Enroll students and email buttons: the reason a button is disabled while the field is empty (the disabled-reason pattern)

rows.o: Add a system prompt in Class settings before you create an experiment
rows.n: Add class instructions in Edit class before you create an experiment.
rows.w: Empty-state frame, disabled call to action: the reason pattern. Phase 3's example; the as-is page has no such precondition, so this ships only if one is added
The neutral in-progress alert (A-18), with American spelling (C18)

rows.n: Only an administrator can change this.
rows.w: A read-only control that only administrators can change: its reason (a pattern)
A read-only value from branding config: its reason (a pattern)
PDF toolbar: Zoom out's reason at the minimum

rows.o: Previous, Next, zoom and fullscreen are unavailable while the document loads
rows.n: These controls are unavailable while the document loads.
rows.w: PDF toolbar: the reason for every inert control while the document loads
DateTimeField: the calendar button's accessible name and tooltip in date mode (the field's own label stays visible and persistent)
DateTimeField: the calendar button's accessible name and tooltip in date and time mode (the field's own label stays visible and persistent)
DateTimeField: the calendar button's accessible name and tooltip in time mode (the field's own label stays visible and persistent)

rows.what: That isn't a date Kiwi can read.
rows.fix: Enter a date like 17 Oct 2026, or choose one in the calendar.
rows.w: DateTimeField, date mode: the field's error when the typed text is not a date (a pattern: what is wrong first, then the correction)

rows.what: That isn't a date and time Kiwi can read.
rows.fix: Enter a date and time like 17 Oct 2026, 14:05, or choose them in the calendar.
rows.w: DateTimeField, date and time mode: the same error

rows.what: That isn't a time Kiwi can read.
rows.fix: Enter a time like 14:05, on the 24-hour clock.
rows.w: DateTimeField, time mode: the same error

rows.fix: Enter a date on or after {min}, or choose one in the calendar.
rows.w: DateTimeField: the error for a value before `min` (the range picker's start date cannot pass its end date)

rows.fix: Enter a date on or before {max}, or choose one in the calendar.
rows.w: DateTimeField: the error for a value after `max`
DateTimeField, date-and-time and time modes: the zone caption under the field, the range picker's own string (`DateTimeRangePicker.tsx:91`), kept for every field that shows a time
Clamped server text (C10) on a touch screen: the visible control, after the text, that lifts the three-line clamp (`aria-expanded`)
rows.t: Hover does not exist on a touch screen, so the full text must not wait behind it. The control shows only on a coarse pointer; the full text stays the accessible description on every pointer.

rows.w: The same control once the message is open
An empty value: the one glyph for "no value" in a table cell, a field or a count (a pattern; a glyph here, not punctuation, C5)
rows.t: One glyph for one meaning (C6): a hyphen, an en dash and an em dash all stood for "no value" on different pages.

rows.w: An empty value's accessible name: the glyph is hidden from assistive technology and "No value" is read in its place (a pattern)
rows.t: A screen reader skips a lone dash or reads it as "dash"; the name says what it means.
